body:
per-run-artifacts-never-removed: Sorted as a defect claim (category defect, no options), but no fix can be correct without a corpus choice, so it routes question.

Evidence, re-verified and still accurate: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-cheatsheet.md:352-364 ("Per-run artifacts and verification stacks") reads "Every verification run mints one fresh tag, builds every artifact it verifies under that tag" and "never any tag that outlives the run, in a verification path". It names no step that removes what a run built. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/review/seed/project.md:27 lists the drive roles stack-start, stack-stop, instance-create, instance-destroy, resource-start, resource-stop, service-log, and sign-in, and none is asked to remove the run's images. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:79 and :114 (Stop the stack) run only stack-stop, instance-destroy, and resource-stop. A grep of plugins/ for rmi, image rm, image prune, and --rmi finds nothing. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md:160 (Ports) covers ports only. The filed problem's site links and quotes still hold. This project itself has no stack (.ok-planner/review/project.md, Drive commands: "No stack"), so the trigger is a consumer project whose verification path builds container images.

Mechanism: the tag is unique to the run, so no later build reuses or replaces its images. Each run adds a full set of images. Nothing removes them, so disk use grows with every drive, certification, and experiment run.

Corpus: decision:per-run-artifact-tag, Choice: "A verification run invokes it once, builds every artifact it verifies under the printed tag, and hands that one value to its verification path". It gives mint, build, and verify, and says nothing about removal. concept:run-tag, Boundaries: "wiring it into builds, stacks, and harnesses is deliberately the project's own change, guided by the rules layer". So the corpus leaves open whether removal belongs to the suite or to the project's own stack commands. That choice decides the fix, so a fixer would have to edit the decision or the concept.

Harm: arguably A5 ("ongoing work ... wears down while the system still looks healthy"): repeated verification runs fill the disk until a build fails. The coverage is weak. A5's sites name repeating work and acquires on a routine path of a long-running process, and a verification run is not long-running. "What the list leaves standing" excludes the machine failing underneath, but here the product causes the disk to fill.

Options:
A. The rules layer tells the project's stack-stop command to remove the artifacts the run built under its tag (for example compose down --rmi local plus removing images tagged with the run tag). Amend the decision's Choice to name removal as the end of the tag's life, and add the duty to the cheatsheet section and to the stack-stop line of seed/project.md. Cost: the duty falls on every project, and a run that crashes before stack-stop still leaks.
B. A, plus the periodic cleanup that the port-block-reads-back-a-stale-record ruling already adds ("A cleanup step, run periodically ... frees each lease whose port nothing holds and whose compose project has no containers left"), widened to remove artifacts carrying a run- tag that no live run holds. Cost: the cleanup must tell a live run's tag from a dead one's and must know the project's artifact kinds (images, build dirs). The retired sketch names this risk: retirement is safe only against tags no live runtime references.
C. A new drive role, such as artifact-remove, that the converge skill runs after stack-stop in drive, confirm, and certification. Cost: one more role every project's project.md must fill, and the audit's experiment runs also need the step.
D. Keep the corpus as it stands: removal is the project's own wiring under concept:run-tag Boundaries, and the cheatsheet gets one sentence saying so. Cost: the rule still leaves the leak open by default.
Also open under any option: whether to keep a failed run's artifacts for debugging.

Siblings: rule with port-block-reads-back-a-stale-record (ruled). Its periodic cleanup and its "Leases end when the run's stack goes down" are the two points where artifact removal would also run. The retired sketch .ok-planner/history/sketches/2026-07-28-verification-cost-and-artifact-lifecycle-sketch.md first named this harm as a retirement policy for superseded tags.
